scams.name: Bird Droppings Pickpocket Scam
scams.description: You're walking along the promenade when suddenly something white and sticky lands on your shoulder. A 'helpful' local appears, offering to clean you up with tissues. While you're distracted and they're wiping your shoulder, their accomplice - or their own nimble fingers - are emptying your pockets or bag. The 'droppings' are actually white paste thrown by a confederate.
scams.avoidance: If substance lands on you, step away from any 'helpers' and handle it yourself. Say 'Non, merci, ça va' and move to a shop or restaurant to clean up. Keep wallet in a front pocket or secure crossbody bag that can't be accessed while distracted.
scams.location: Streets near Grande Plage, Promenade du Casino, Avenue Edouard VII, pedestrian areas

scams.name: Beach Blanket Theft at Grande Plage
scams.description: You've left your belongings on your beach towel while going for a quick swim in the Atlantic. A thief has been watching and waiting. They casually stroll past your blanket, scoop up your phone, wallet, and keys, and disappear into the crowd before you've noticed. Beach theft spikes during July and August when Grande Plage is packed.
scams.avoidance: Never leave valuables unattended on the beach - use a waterproof pouch to take essentials into the water. Leave passport, excess cash, and electronics in your hotel safe. Swim in shifts with companions so someone always watches belongings.
scams.location: Grande Plage, Plage Miramar, Cote des Basques, beach areas during peak summer season

scams.name: Camera Drop Scam
scams.description: A friendly tourist asks if you'd take their photo with their nice camera. As you hand it back, they fumble it dramatically and it crashes to the ground. They examine their 'broken' camera and demand you pay for the damage - €200-300 or more. The camera was already broken or is a cheap prop; this is a practiced routine.
scams.avoidance: It's fine to take photos for tourists, but hand the camera back carefully. If they drop it, remember the fumble was on their end. Never pay cash on the spot; suggest involving police if they claim damage. Walk away if they become aggressive.
scams.location: Rocher de la Vierge viewpoint, Port Vieux, Grande Plage promenade, popular photo spots

scams.name: ATM Card Skimming and Shoulder Surfing
scams.description: Someone approaches at an ATM offering helpful advice while watching you enter your PIN and potentially scanning your card's magnetic strip with a skimmer in their pocket. Or they've already installed a skimmer on the ATM slot itself. Days later, your account shows unauthorized withdrawals in eastern Europe.
scams.avoidance: Use ATMs inside banks during business hours where tampering is less likely. Cover the keypad completely with your hand when entering your PIN. Check the card slot by wiggling it gently - skimmers are often loosely attached. Never accept help from strangers at ATMs.
scams.location: ATMs near Casino Barriere, Avenue Edouard VII, Les Halles market area, train station

scams.name: Shell Game and Three-Card Monte
scams.description: You spot a crowd gathered around a man with three boxes or cards on a folding table. He's shuffling rapidly, inviting people to guess which one hides the ball. Someone 'wins' €20 - but those 'winners' are accomplices. The moment you bet, sleight of hand ensures you lose. And while you're focused on the game, a pickpocket may be working the crowd.
scams.avoidance: Never gamble with street operators - the games are rigged without exception. Walk past quickly without stopping to watch. Remember that every 'winner' you see is a plant working with the scammer. Keep hands on your valuables even if you pause nearby.
scams.location: Casino promenade, Grande Plage boardwalk, near Rocher de la Vierge during peak tourist season

scams.name: Friendly Bar Overcharging Scam
scams.description: Two attractive locals strike up a friendly conversation and suggest continuing over drinks at a place they know nearby. After a couple of drinks, the bill arrives: €150-200 or more. The drinks were massively inflated 'tourist prices,' and your 'friends' chip in only a token amount before disappearing. Large bouncers may escort you to an ATM to pay.
scams.avoidance: Choose your own venues - never let strangers guide you to a bar they recommend. Always check prices before ordering; no posted prices is a massive red flag. If confronted with an outrageous bill, insist on calling police before paying.
scams.location: Bars near Port Vieux, late-night establishments in city center, venues off main tourist streets

scams.name: Les Halles Market Pickpocketing
scams.description: Les Halles is a beloved Biarritz institution where locals and tourists jostle to buy fresh seafood and regional specialties. The crowded aisles and sensory overload make it a prime hunting ground for skilled pickpockets. While you're admiring the piment d'Espelette display, a bump passes unnoticed - and your wallet goes with it.
scams.avoidance: Wear a crossbody bag with the opening against your body, hand resting on top. Keep wallet in a front pocket, never in a backpack or rear pocket. Bring only the cash you need for market purchases. Be extra vigilant during peak Saturday morning hours.
scams.location: Les Halles de Biarritz indoor market, Saturday morning market, Rue des Halles area

scams.name: Unlicensed Taxi Overcharging
scams.description: A friendly man at the airport exit offers a taxi into town and quotes €40 - but this isn't an official taxi. Once you're in the car, the price mysteriously increases, or you're taken on a scenic route. Official airport taxis should cost around €25 to central Biarritz. Unlicensed operators charge double or triple the standard fare.
scams.avoidance: Use only official taxis from the designated taxi rank at the airport or station. Look for official taxi signage, license numbers, and running meters. Know the expected fare in advance: airport to city center is approximately €25. Use ride-hailing apps for transparent pricing.
scams.location: Biarritz-Pays Basque Airport (BIQ), Biarritz train station, late-night casino area

scams.name: Fake Charity Petition Scam
scams.description: A young woman approaches with a clipboard, gesturing that she's deaf-mute. She wants you to sign a petition for disabled children or another worthy cause. Once signed, she flips to a donation page showing €20-50 amounts. Meanwhile, your attention is on the clipboard, making you an easy mark for an accomplice to pickpocket. The charity doesn't exist.
scams.avoidance: Politely decline with 'Non, merci' and keep walking without breaking stride. Never sign anything on the street; legitimate charities don't solicit signatures on promenades. Keep your hands occupied so you can't take the clipboard.
scams.location: Grande Plage promenade, Place Clemenceau, near the casino, pedestrian shopping areas

scams.name: Remote Beach and Parking Lot Car Break-Ins
scams.description: You've driven to one of Biarritz's stunning remote beaches. You leave your rental car with bags hidden in the boot. Thieves stake out these beach parking areas, watching tourists head to the water. Within minutes, they've smashed a window or popped a lock. Valuables 'hidden' in the boot are found quickly.
scams.avoidance: Leave all valuables at your hotel - don't bring anything to the beach you can't carry into the water. Use paid, supervised parking lots rather than remote free parking. Put items in the boot BEFORE arriving at the beach (thieves watch people hide things).
scams.location: Cote des Basques parking lot, Plage de la Milady parking, remote surf spot access roads, cliffside parking areas

scams.name: Surf Equipment Rental Damage Claims
scams.description: You rent a surfboard from one of the many rental stands along Biarritz's beaches. When you return it, the operator scrutinizes the board and 'discovers' a ding or crack that they claim you caused. They demand €50-100 for repairs. The damage may have been pre-existing and hidden, or it may be standard wear they use to extract money.
scams.avoidance: Before accepting any rental equipment, photograph it from all angles with your phone's timestamp visible. Ask the operator to note any existing damage on the rental agreement. Use established, well-reviewed rental companies rather than informal beach stands.
scams.location: Surf rental shops along Grande Plage, Cote des Basques equipment hire, beachfront rental stands

scams.name: Bus and Public Transport Pickpocketing
scams.description: Biarritz's Chronoplus buses are generally safe, but pickpockets target crowded routes serving beaches and tourist areas. During the press of boarding or when standing in a packed bus during summer, a skilled thief slips a hand into your bag or pocket. They often work in pairs: one bumps or distracts, the other steals.
scams.avoidance: Keep bags zipped and held in front of you, not hanging off your shoulder. Use a money belt for passport and large amounts of cash. Keep phone in a front pocket, not a loose jacket pocket. Stay alert when boarding and exiting.
scams.location: Bus lines serving Grande Plage and city center, crowded Chronoplus buses, train station platforms
